proposals.before: Ruizong, styled the Emperor Jingxiang, bore the personal name Tolui and was the fourth son of Taizu and uterine younger brother of Taizong.
proposals.after: Ruizong, the Emperor Jingxiang, bore the personal name Tolui and was the fourth son of Taizu and uterine younger brother of Taizong.
proposals.reason: 景襄皇帝 is a posthumous imperial designation, not a courtesy style (表字); 'styled' misrepresents 睿宗景襄皇帝，諱拖雷.

proposals.before: His consort was Sorghaghtani Beki of the Kereit.
proposals.after: His consort was of the Kereit clan.
proposals.reason: Chinese 妃怯烈氏 names only the consort's Kereit clan affiliation; the idiomatic English invents the personal name Sorghaghtani Beki.

proposals.before: When Xianzong took the throne he posthumously enfeoffed him as the Emperor Yingwu with temple name Ruizong.
proposals.after: When Xianzong took the throne he posthumously styled him the Emperor Yingwu with temple name Ruizong.
proposals.reason: 追謚 means posthumous titling/styling, not enfeoffment; 'enfeoffed' mistranslates the verb.

proposals.before: Yuzong, styled the Emperor Wenhui Mingxiao, bore the personal name Zhenjin and was Shizu's son by the principal wife.
proposals.after: Yuzong, the Emperor Wenhui Mingxiao, bore the personal name Zhenjin and was Shizu's son by the principal wife.
proposals.reason: 文惠明孝皇帝 is a posthumous title, not a style name; 'styled' misstates the naming category.

proposals.before: His mother was Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng of the Onggirat, Chabi.
proposals.after: His mother was Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng of the Onggirat.
proposals.reason: Chinese names only 昭睿順聖皇后 and 弘吉烈氏; 'Chabi' is invented and absent from the source sentence.

proposals.before: In an interval he said to the princes Zhalaqu and the attendant officials Bayan and others: "We happen to have this leisure; each of you should lay open your hearts, speak carefully of what you uphold, and let me hear it."
proposals.after: In an interval he said to Prince Zhalaqu and the attendant officials Bayan and others: "We happen to have this leisure; each of you should lay open your hearts, speak carefully of what you uphold, and let me hear it."
proposals.reason: 諸王劄剌忽 denotes one prince titled 諸王; plural 'princes Zhalaqu' invents multiple persons.

proposals.before: If anyone obstructs, I shall uphold you with force."
proposals.after: If anyone obstructs, I shall firmly uphold you."
proposals.reason: 力持之 means firmly uphold/support, not physical force; with force mistranslates 力.

proposals.before: When he heard that Han Emperor Cheng did not close the imperial carriage road and that Tang Emperor Suzong changed the crimson gauze robe to vermilion-bright dress, he said with delight, "If I acted on these, I would do the same."
proposals.after: When he heard that Han Emperor Cheng did not cut across the imperial carriage road and that Tang Emperor Suzong changed the crimson gauze robe to vermilion-bright dress, he said with delight, "If I acted on these, I would do the same."
proposals.reason: 不絕馳道 means not traversing/cutting across the reserved imperial highway, not closing it.

proposals.before: The Crown Prince heard that Han Emperor Cheng did not close the imperial carriage road and that Tang Emperor Suzong changed the crimson gauze robe to the vermilion-bright robe; he said with great pleasure: "If I put these into practice, I too would do likewise."
proposals.after: The Crown Prince heard that Han Emperor Cheng did not cut across the imperial carriage road and that Tang Emperor Suzong changed the crimson gauze robe to the vermilion-bright robe; he said with great pleasure: "If I put these into practice, I too would do likewise."
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 絕馳道 is cutting across the highway, not closing it.

proposals.before: He once said, "I hear that under Jin Emperor Zhangzong, officials said National University students' stipends were too costly. Zhangzong replied that nurturing one Fan Zhongyan repaid the cost. His words were excellent.
proposals.after: He once said, "I hear that under Jin Emperor Zhangzong, officials said National University students' stipends were too costly. Zhangzong replied that nurturing one Fan Zhongyan repaid the cost.
proposals.reason: The clause 'His words were excellent' translates 其言甚善, which belongs to the next unit s0150, not to s0149.

proposals.before: Junior Mentor Bo Bi brought his son Abachi to audience; he instructed him to enter study; Bo Bi at once sent his son into Mongolian study.
proposals.after: Junior Mentor Bo Bi brought his son Abachi to audience; the Crown Prince instructed him to enter study; Bo Bi at once sent his son into Mongolian study.
proposals.reason: Silent subject of 諭令入學 is the crown prince, not Bo Bi; the literal 'he' wrongly leaves the instructor ambiguous.

proposals.before: More than a year later he saw him again and asked what book he was reading. The son answered in Mongolian script. The crown prince said, "I ordered you to study Chinese writing. Enter the Imperial College at once."
proposals.after: More than a year later he saw him again and asked what book he was reading. The son answered that he was reading Mongolian writing. The crown prince said, "I ordered you to study Chinese writing. Enter the Imperial College at once."
proposals.reason: 以蒙古書對 means he replied that his reading was Mongolian writing/books, not that he answered using Mongolian script.

proposals.before: More than a year later he saw him again; the Crown Prince asked what book he was reading; the son answered in Mongolian script; the Crown Prince said: "I ordered you to study Chinese writing — enter the Imperial College at once."
proposals.after: More than a year later he saw him again; the Crown Prince asked what book he was reading; the son answered that he was reading Mongolian writing; the Crown Prince said: "I ordered you to study Chinese writing — enter the Imperial College at once."
proposals.reason: Same error as idiomatic: 以蒙古書對 reports the content of the reply (Mongolian writings), not the script used to answer.

proposals.before: Xianzong, styled the Emperor Guang Sheng Renxiao, bore the personal name Gammala and was the eldest son of Yuzong.
proposals.after: Xianzong, styled the Emperor Guangsheng Renxiao, bore the personal name Gammala and was the eldest son of Yuzong.
proposals.reason: 光聖仁孝 is one posthumous compound; splitting Guang Sheng as separate English words obscures the name.

proposals.before: He had three sons. The eldest was Amuge, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, a son by adoption.
proposals.after: He had three sons. The eldest was Amuge, enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, born of Guo.
proposals.reason: Chinese 郭出也 means born of Guo (the maid Guo), not adoption; the idiomatic English invents adoptive status.

proposals.before: He had three sons: the eldest was Amuge, enfeoffed Prince of Wei — a son by adoption;
proposals.after: He had three sons: the eldest was Amuge, enfeoffed Prince of Wei — born of Guo;
proposals.reason: Chinese 郭出也 means born of Guo; the literal English wrongly renders it as adoption.

decisions.reason: 睿宗景襄皇帝 juxtaposes the temple name with the posthumous title 景襄皇帝; 'styled' wrongly treats that title as a courtesy style (表字).
妃怯烈氏 records only that the consort was of the Kereit clan; the personal name Sorghaghtani Beki is not in the Chinese.
追謚曰英武皇帝 is posthumous titling (謚), not a grant of fief; 'enfeoffed' mistranslates the verb.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 追謚曰英武皇帝，廟號睿宗

decisions.reason: 文惠明孝皇帝 is the posthumous imperial designation after 裕宗, not a courtesy style; removing 'styled' restores the naming category.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 裕宗文惠明孝皇帝，諱真金

decisions.reason: 母昭睿順聖皇后，弘吉烈氏 names the posthumous title and Onggirat clan only; Chabi is absent from this sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 母昭睿順聖皇后，弘吉烈氏

decisions.reason: 諸王劄剌忽 is one person titled 諸王 plus the name 劄剌忽; plural 'princes Zhalaqu' invents multiple princes.
力持之 uses 力 adverbially as firmly/strenuously upholding support, not wielding physical force; the proposed rendering matches the Chinese.
不絕馳道 means he did not cut across/traverse the reserved imperial carriage road; 'close' invents a different action.
Same Chinese 不絕馳道: 絕 means cutting across the chi-dao, not closing the road.
s0149 ends at 所償顧豈少哉; 其言甚善 belongs to the next unit s0150, so the idiomatic must not absorb that clause.
After 入見, silent 諭令入學 is the crown prince's instruction; s0154's 我命汝學 confirms the speaker, so ambiguous 'he' must be clarified.
太子問讀何書，其子以蒙古書對 answers the question of what book he was reading with Mongolian writings, not that he replied in Mongolian script.
Same 以蒙古書對: the reply's content is Mongolian writing/books, matching the question 讀何書.

decisions.after: Xianzong, the Emperor Guangsheng Renxiao, bore the personal name Gammala and was the eldest son of Yuzong.
decisions.reason: 光聖仁孝皇帝 is a posthumous title, so 'styled' is wrong as in parallel openings, and 光聖 should be the single English compound Guangsheng rather than split Guang Sheng.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 顯宗光聖仁孝皇帝，諱甘麻剌

decisions.reason: 郭出也 means born of Guo, contrasting with 妃所生者 in the next sentence; 'son by adoption' invents adoptive status absent from the Chinese.
Same 郭出也: the literal must read born of Guo, not adoption.

claimRetractions.reason: Accepted r0002 shows the personal name Sorghaghtani Beki was invented by the bad idiomatic; 妃怯烈氏 supports only the clan affiliation claim.
Accepted r0005 shows English Chabi was supplied only by the bad translation; s0071 names 昭睿順聖皇后 and 弘吉烈氏 alone.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 母昭睿順聖皇后，弘吉烈氏

claimRevisions.reason: Revised r0014 restores 光聖 as the English compound Guangsheng; the posthumous-name claim must not keep the split Guang Sheng form.
Revised r0014 likewise requires the honor label English to read Guangsheng Renxiao while keeping zh, id, subject, predicate, and evidence.
